reason: JS spread semantics genuinely copy an own `type` property whose value is `undefined`, so `{ type: "string", ...schema.propertyNames }` does clobber the injected default in exactly the case the guard `schema.propertyNames.type === undefined` admits, and such an object is constructible by a caller (e.g. spreading another schema); the code's own comment confirms the resulting key schema would degrade to `z.any()`, though this edge case is unlikely for JSON-parsed input and remains unchanged after the fix.
